summary: Both sides draw a morphing cellular wall-network with full-spectrum saturated hue cycling at a matching ~3 s rate, but the port's cells are roughly an order of magnitude too large and scale with the canvas, while the original's honeycomb has a pixel-locked ~4.6 px cell pitch — on the default 16x16 rig the original is dense multicolour speckle and the port is one or two soft blobs.
observations: Neither side exposes any controls (meta.json sides.orig.controls = [] and sides.port.controls = []; --probe-controls reports '(no settable controls)' for both). No control-surface mismatch.
Neither side binds sensors (wantsSensors false on both, sensors 'off'). Neither side reports a compile or runtime error in any of the 22 runs performed.

Both sides are seed-independent: --seed 1234 (label seed1234) produced statsSummary byte-for-byte identical to --seed 1 (baseline): orig meanBrightness avg 38.9 vs 39.9, motion avg 5.8 vs 7.3 differ only through the different window; the frame content is deterministic and the pattern is not random-driven.

SPATIAL SCALE IS THE HEADLINE DIVERGENCE. 1-D spatial DFT of mid row and mid column, averaged over 24 lines per frame, sampled at 40 times across 0-58.6 s on a 96x96 grid (label hc-scan96): original spectral centroid averages k=15.9 cycles/canvas (peak k wanders 1-32 as the pattern breathes); port centroid averages k=5.9 with the PEAK pinned at k=1-2 in all 40 frames. The port never draws more than about two cells per axis; the original never drops below about 9.

RESOLUTION BEHAVIOUR DIFFERS STRUCTURALLY. Same instant (t=21 s) rendered at --grid 32x32 / 48x48 / 96x96 / 192x192 (labels res32/res48/res96/res192): original centroid k = 7.5 / 10.3 / 19.7 / 41.9 cycles per canvas, i.e. 0.23 / 0.21 / 0.21 / 0.22 cycles per PIXEL — a constant honeycomb cell pitch of ~4.6 device pixels at every grid size. Port peak k = 1 at all four grid sizes (centroid 3.5 / 4.3 / 6.6 / 10.7, the rise being extra resolved harmonics of its soft glow, not extra cells). The original rasterizes in pixel units; the port draws into a normalized canvas.

ON THE DEFAULT 16x16 RIG the original is aliased below its own Nyquist and renders as incoherent per-pixel speckle: a --dump of frames at t=0, 0.05, 0.1, 3, 6, 9 s (label dump0) shows adjacent pixels swinging between 0 and ~250 with no smooth gradient anywhere. The port at the same times shows large smooth gradients — a single blob or ring filling most of the 16x16 frame. A viewer on the shipping rig sees shimmering multicolour noise from the original and slow soft blobs from the port.

De-aliased at 96x96 (label grid96, 60 s / 5 fps) the original is unmistakably a honeycomb: a dense lattice of ~12-16 outlined hex/diamond cells per axis in offset rows, morphing in aspect ratio and shear over time. In the coarse-scale regime (label regime-coarse, --skip 21) the original still shows ~12x12 cells across the canvas while the port at the same instant shows a SINGLE huge magenta/blue arc covering the frame.

In the port's finest regime (label regime-fine, --skip 5, 96x96) the port shows a ~2x2 lattice of rounded squares with small circles at the vertices — a square (4-fold) cell lattice, not a hexagonal honeycomb tiling. The original at the same instant is a lattice of 30+ narrow cells per axis.

The port's cell walls are broad gaussian glows (~8-12 px wide on a 96 px canvas, ~10% of the canvas); the original's walls are ~1-2 px on the same canvas. Relative to each side's own cell size the wall duty is comparable (~20-25%), so this follows mostly from the scale error rather than being an independent defect.

TEMPORAL RATE MATCHES. Temporal DFT of the 60 s / 5 fps 96x96 series: both sides carry a dominant ~0.30-0.37 Hz component (period ~3 s) in meanBrightness and in all three colour channels, plus a slow 0.02-0.08 Hz palette drift. The port is not too fast or too slow.

BOTH SIDES ARE TIME-BASED, no frame-rate coupling divergence. meanR from --seconds 60 --fps 5 (survey) resampled against --seconds 60 --fps 20 (label long20) aligns in SECONDS on both sides: mean abs diff 5.33 (orig) and 4.44 (port) on a 0-97 range, entirely accounted for by the shared one-frame pre-advance (5 fps is 1/5-1/20 = 0.15 s ahead on both sides). The raw `motion` triple at 10/20/40 fps (labels fps10/fps20/fps40, 96x96) is misleading here — orig 50/51/45 is saturated by its high spatial frequency, port 7/4/2 simply halves with the frame delta.

COLOUR FAMILY IS COMPARABLE, port slightly dimmer and cooler. Over the 40 sampled 96x96 frames both sides are fully saturated (meanSat 1.00 on both) and both light a similar fraction of the rig (v>0.15 on 48.1% of pixels for orig, 46.5% for port), with about 5 of 12 hue bins present per frame on each. Original hue histogram skews warm (0-180 deg holds 66.7% of lit pixels), port is near-uniform with a cool lean (180-360 deg holds 53.8%). Mean value of lit pixels: orig 158, port 125 — the port runs ~20% dimmer, consistent with whole-rig meanBrightness 39.3 vs 31.3 over the 60 s survey.

STEADY STATE IS HEALTHY ON BOTH. brightnessTrend 'steady' on both sides in every run; --skip 120 --seconds 30 --fps 10 (label late) gives orig meanBrightness avg 38.8 / motion avg 11.7 / zeroMotionFrames 0 and port 31.8 / 9.2 / 0. Neither side decays, freezes or saturates; the port is not time-degenerate.

The survey rhythm images tell the same story from far away: the original's rhythm is a fine high-frequency zigzag (~14-16 spatial cycles across the width, rapid temporal oscillation), the port's is 2-3 broad slow waves.
feedback: The single fix that matters is spatial scale. The port draws 1-2 cells per axis; the original draws roughly 12-16 per axis on a 96x96 canvas. Multiply the port's cell frequency by ~8-10x and the two become the same picture at the same instant.

The original's cell pitch is fixed in DEVICE PIXELS (~4.6 px per cell, measured constant at 0.21-0.23 cycles/pixel across 32x32, 48x48, 96x96 and 192x192 renders), whereas the port's is a fixed fraction of the canvas (peak k=1 at all four sizes). Whatever coordinate the port feeds its lattice is normalized where the original's is in pixel units — the port needs to scale its coordinates by the grid dimension so that cell size stops tracking the canvas.

Consequence to check after the fix: on the default 16x16 rig the original is BELOW Nyquist for its own lattice and correctly renders as dense saturated per-pixel speckle, not as a visible honeycomb. A fixed port must reproduce that speckle on 16x16, not a smooth pattern — verify the fix at 96x96 (where the honeycomb should be visible with ~12-16 cells per axis) AND at 16x16 (where it should look like noise).

The port's lattice topology is a square 4-fold arrangement of rounded cells with circles at the vertices; the original's is an offset/staggered arrangement of elongated hexagons and diamonds. Once the scale is right, check the cell tiling geometry too — a honeycomb should have row-to-row stagger.

The port's cell walls are much softer than the original's. At 96x96 the port's wall is an ~8-12 px gaussian glow; the original's is a ~1-2 px hard-edged outline. Tighten the falloff after the scale fix (some of this will resolve automatically once the cells shrink).
Brightness: the port's lit pixels average value 125 against the original's 158 (whole-rig mean 31 vs 39 over 60 s). Raise the port's output by ~25% once structure matches.

Hue distribution: the original spends about two thirds of its lit pixels in the warm half of the wheel (0-180 deg), the port is near-uniform with a slight cool lean. Both are fully saturated with a ~3 s hue cycle, so only the bias needs adjusting; the cycle rate is already correct and should not be touched.

Do NOT change the animation rate. The ~0.30-0.37 Hz morph and the ~0.02-0.08 Hz palette drift already match, both sides are time-based (fps-invariant), both are seed-independent, and neither side decays over a 150 s window.
